+import Std.Tactic
+
+/-!
+Generic arithmetic behind `NativeCyclicRotation.shiftDigits` at half a radix.
+This standalone module uses Lean 4.32.0 core/Std only. It changes neither the
+cyclic predecessor nor any definition in the source repository.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofReview
+
+theorem half_shift_formula {s : Nat} (hs : 0 < s) (a b : Nat) :
+    (s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s) = s * (a % 2) + b / 2 := by
+  rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 s, Nat.mul_mod_mul_left, Nat.mul_div_mul_left _ _ hs]
+
+/-- Only the predecessor digit needs a bound; the current digit is arbitrary. -/
+theorem half_shift_bound {s a b : Nat} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : b ≤ 3) :
+    (s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s) ≤ s + 1 := by
+  rw [half_shift_formula hs]
+  have ha : a % 2 ≤ 1 := by omega
+  have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left s ha
+  omega
+
+/-- Even scale kills the low contribution modulo two. -/
+theorem half_shift_parity {s a b : Nat} (hs : 0 < s)
+    (heven : s % 2 = 0) (hb : b ≤ 3) :
+    ((s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s)) % 2 = b / 2 := by
+  rw [half_shift_formula hs]
+  simp only [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, heven, Nat.zero_mul, Nat.zero_mod,
+    Nat.zero_add, Nat.mod_mod]
+  exact Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (show b / 2 < 2 by omega)
+
+#print axioms half_shift_formula
+#print axioms half_shift_bound
+#print axioms half_shift_parity
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofReview

+import Std.Tactic
+
+/-!
+Scalar interface for an exact natural digit/carry decomposition. These lemmas
+support the existing `Facts` interface; they do not assume a zero incoming
+carry and do not impose any cyclic starting point.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofReview
+
+theorem quotient_of_decomposition {raw digit carry radix : Nat}
+    (hd : digit < radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) :
+    carry = raw / radix := by
+  rw [h, Nat.add_mul_div_left _ _ (show 0 < radix by omega),
+    Nat.div_eq_of_lt hd, Nat.zero_add]
+
+theorem residue_of_decomposition {raw digit carry radix modulus : Nat}
+    (hm : modulus ∣ radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) :
+    digit % modulus = raw % modulus := by
+  rw [h, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd hm]
+  simp only [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.zero_mod, Nat.add_zero, Nat.mod_mod]
+
+/-- A small raw total resets its outgoing carry. No digit bound is needed. -/
+theorem zero_carry_of_decomposition {raw digit carry radix : Nat}
+    (hsmall : raw < radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) : carry = 0 := by
+  have hd : digit < radix := by omega
+  exact (quotient_of_decomposition hd h).trans (Nat.div_eq_of_lt hsmall)
+
+#print axioms quotient_of_decomposition
+#print axioms residue_of_decomposition
+#print axioms zero_carry_of_decomposition
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofReview

+    {g : List.Vector Nat (n + 2) → Nat}
+    (p : PRCode.Realizes f) (q : PRCode.Realizes g) :
+    PRCode.Realizes (fun v : List.Vector Nat (n + 1) =>
+      v.head.rec (f v.tail) (fun i acc => g (i ::ᵥ acc ::ᵥ v.tail))) := by
+  refine ⟨.prec p.val q.val, ?_⟩
+  intro v

+theorem total_le_one_all_phases_exists (bit digit : ℕ → ℕ)
+    {k b phase epsilon clause : ℕ}
+    (hbit : ∀ j, j < 942 → bit j ≤ 1)
+    (hk : k ≤ 57) (hb : b ≤ 1) (hepsilon : epsilon ≤ 1)
+    (hresidue : clause % 2048 =
+      (2 * prefixSum bit 942 + k + b + 2 ^ phase * epsilon) % 2048)
+    (hmask : clause &&& (2 ^ 45 - 4) = 0)
+    (hpadding : 7 ≤ phase → phase ≤ 10 → ∃ u : ℕ → ℕ,
+      (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ 483 → u j ≤ 2) ∧
+      (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ 483 →
+        digit j % 16 = (2 * prefixSum bit j + u j) % 16) ∧
+      (∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ 483 → digit j &&& 8 = 0)) :
+    prefixSum bit 942 ≤ 1 := by
+  have hn : prefixSum bit 942 ≤ 942 := by
+    have hh := prefix_add_le bit 0 942 (fun j _ hj => hbit j (by omega))
+    simpa only [zero_add, prefix_zero] using hh
+  by_cases hsmall : phase ≤ 6
+  · exact count_small_phase hn hk hb hsmall hepsilon hresidue hmask
+  by_cases hmiddle : phase ≤ 10
+  · obtain ⟨u, hu, hr, hm⟩ := hpadding (by omega) hmiddle
+    have hn' := total_le_462 bit u digit hbit hu hr hm
+    have hp : 2 ^ phase ≤ 1024 := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide) hmiddle
+    have ht : 2 ^ phase * epsilon ≤ 1024 := by
+      have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (2 ^ phase) hepsilon
+      omega

+  · exact count_large_phase hn hk hb (by omega) hresidue hmask

+import DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticDAGPowers
+
+/-! A proposed relation for circuit-translation certificates. Subtraction
+remains ordered; only addition and multiplication allow operand exchange. -/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.RefactoringReview
+open ArithmeticDAG
+
+variable {inputs fixed : ℕ}
+
+def NodeRelComm (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) : Node inputs fixed → Node inputs fixed → Prop
+  | .add a b, .add c d | .mul a b, .mul c d =>
+      (rel a c ∧ rel b d) ∨ (rel a d ∧ rel b c)
+  | n, m => NodeRel rel n m
+
+instance (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) [DecidableRel rel] (n m : Node inputs fixed) :
+    Decidable (NodeRelComm rel n m) := by
+  cases n <;> cases m <;> simp only [NodeRelComm, NodeRel] <;> infer_instance
+
+theorem evalAt_of_NodeRelComm {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
+    (p : Fin fixed → R) (x : Fin inputs → R)
+    (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) (old new : Node inputs fixed) (v w : ℕ → R)
+    (h : NodeRelComm rel old new) (hv : ∀ i j, rel i j → w j = v i) :
+    new.evalAt p x w = old.evalAt p x v := by
+  cases old <;> cases new <;> simp_all [NodeRelComm, NodeRel, Node.evalAt]
+  all_goals first
+    | (rcases h with h | h
+       · rw [hv _ _ h.1, hv _ _ h.2]
+       · rw [hv _ _ h.2, hv _ _ h.1]
+         first | exact add_comm _ _ | exact mul_comm _ _)
+    | rw [hv _ _ h.1, hv _ _ h.2]
+
+#print axioms evalAt_of_NodeRelComm
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.RefactoringReview

+The half-radix cases of \code{NativeCyclicRotation.shiftDigits} reduce to the exact identity, for $s>0$,

+R=d+B c,\qquad 0\le d<B.

+\section{Object-language proofs: remove administration, retain definability}

+\subsection{A definable-induction transport lemma}

+\section{Automation and performance: a measured workflow}
+
+\subsection{Prefer a stable simplification boundary}
+
+The most maintainable short proofs usually unfold one semantic layer and use named facts for the next. Keep executable code, expression evaluation, arithmetic normal forms and model interpretation as separate simplification layers. A proof which unfolds every implementation at once may be shorter in source while producing larger goals and coupling distant modules.
+
+Use \code{simp?} during development to discover a sufficient explicit set; retain \code{simp only} where stable dependencies matter. The Lean manual documents both the explicit set and ordinary simplifier behavior.\footnote{\url{https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The-Simplifier/Invoking-the-Simplifier/}; accessed 26 October 2026. Exact examples in this packet were checked against Lean 4.32.0.} Do not mechanically replace every \code{simp} with a long explicit list. Small, conventional algebraic normalizations are often clearer with the ordinary simplifier.
+
+Use \code{omega} for bounded natural/integer arithmetic after the mathematical structure is exposed. Use \code{ring} for algebraic identities, \code{nlinarith} where inequalities genuinely need nonlinear combination, and \code{decide +kernel} for closed finite certificates when appropriate. Replacing all proofs by broad automation would obscure the very interfaces this report recommends.
+
+\subsection{Measure four distinct things}
+
+For a proposed refactor, record source size, elaboration/kernel-checking time, proof-object size if relevant, and dependency impact. They can move in different directions. A 1,650-line source reduction says nothing by itself about a 25\% time saving. Similarly, a larger generic theorem can make dozens of client proofs clearer without reducing the first migrated file.
+
+Profile a representative old and new theorem under the same toolchain, imports and cache state. Separate cold dependency builds from repeated theorem elaboration. Use a wall-clock command around Lean and, when needed, \code{set_option trace.profiler true} locally to identify which phase consumes time. Retain the underlying command and output, rather than inferring performance from heartbeat limits or one noisy parallel run.
+
+\subsection{Keep the proof trust visible}
+
+The new examples use ordinary proof-producing tactics and include axiom reports. A source reduction should not obtain its apparent simplicity by adding \code{sorry}, assuming the desired correctness theorem, or substituting native computation for the existing trust policy. The official Lean manual explains that native evaluation introduces an additional trust dependency beyond kernel proof checking.\footnote{\url{https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Axioms/}. The packet's actual \code{#print axioms} output, on the pinned version, is the relevant evidence for each checked example.}
+
+Do not turn finite data verification into an unlinked Python assertion. Python is useful for generating and auditing labels; a Lean theorem must still bind those labels to the actual circuit data. Conversely, the static scripts in this archive are deliberately labelled as static checks, not replacements for Lean.
+
+\section{Validation status and reproduction}
+
+\input{validation-table.tex}
+
+The examples are separate namespace additions and proof replacements prepared outside the original source tree. There was no remote commit or pull request. The compilation receipts cover the listed examples and complete modified files only; they are not an all-module build of the 546-file subtree. The source-only candidate files are clearly labelled.
+

+
+Use the pinned commit and toolchain in an isolated checkout. The packaged scripts accept explicit paths. The generated-circuit auditor compares the public statements byte for byte and independently checks the literal circuit label conditions. +
+The replay script checks the commit and toolchain, builds only the dependencies selected by the included Lean imports, compiles each demonstration, records return codes, and saves output. It does not apply any candidate patch automatically. The README provides the separate static-generator and patch-check commands. Building from an empty cache can require substantial dependency downloads; the saved proof-check logs are included for immediate inspection.
+
+\subsection{Adoption sequence}
+
+\begin{enumerate}
+\item Take the proof-body-only recursion patch. Rebuild its direct users and retain the program-data equality checks.
+\item Take the list-library patch and assignment naturality change. Keep wrapper signatures, witness counts and expression data unchanged.
+\item Add the shared SOS and topological-invariant theorems in modules low enough in the import graph. Migrate a small number of clients before expanding usage.
+\item Update the circuit source generator, regenerate both Steps modules, compile the finite certificates and replay downstream Registers/Recipe/Translation modules. Compare public types and literal data hashes.
+\item Introduce scanner helpers and conditional padding existence. For the latter, check every caller because its interface changes.
+\item Consolidate digit/carry and model-theoretic interfaces in separate changes. These require careful attention to bounds, cyclic semantics, definability and logical contexts.
+\end{enumerate}
+
+Each stage should remain understandable on its own. It is preferable to land a small correct interface with a few clients than to combine proof shortening, program optimization, theorem generalization and a new mathematical endpoint in one patch.
+
+\section{Further questions worth investigating}
+
+\begin{enumerate}
+\item \textbf{What is the best certificate granularity?} Compare a single power-label certificate, fixed-size chunks, and per-node certificates. Keep the actual circuit list fixed and measure kernel time, memory and source size together.
+\item \textbf{Can one translation interface cover later circuit variants?} Test the commutative local relation and explicit input/output correspondence on both current families before designing a larger compiler framework.
+\item \textbf{Which scanner properties are truly shared?} Fixed-state laws are immediately reusable; encoded-list simulations need a precise relation between row storage, raw zero states and semantic histories. Determine the smallest interface that serves all four scanners.
+\item \textbf{Can degree proofs be mostly certificate driven?} Separate purely structural bounds from cancellation-sensitive normal forms and exact-degree witnesses. Measure how many manual degree chains remain after this classification.
+\item \textbf{How many object-language endpoints share one completeness bridge?} Inventory empty versus nonempty contexts and definability requirements before choosing the generic statement. A bridge should make these assumptions more explicit.
+\item \textbf{Where does build time actually go?} After the small proof replacements, profile the large generated and finite classification modules. This can establish whether evaluator representation or certificate sharding is worth the wider refactor.
+\end{enumerate}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Prepare non-mutating Steps refactor candidates from pinned Lean source.
+
+The generator derives exponent labels from existing theorem statements. A
+Lean PowerStep certificate rechecks all labels against the literal circuit;
+the generator is not part of the mathematical trust boundary.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+
+FAMILIES = (
+    ("GapCircuitSteps66", "GapCircuit66", 11, 484, 20),
+    ("SplitCircuitSteps59", "SplitCircuit59", 12, 515, 36),
+)
+
+
+def render(source, module, circuit, fixed, length, base):
+    power_re = re.compile(
+        r"theorem natural_power_(\d+) (\(p : Fin \d+ → R\) \(x : Fin 9 → R\) :\n"
+        r"    naturalRegister p x \d+ = naturalRegister p x (\d+) \^ (\d+)) := by\n"
+        r".*?(?=\ntheorem |\nend )", re.S)
+    matches = list(power_re.finditer(source))
+    assert matches, module
+    labels = [0] * length
+    labels[base] = 1
+    for m in matches:
+        assert int(m[3]) == base
+        labels[int(m[1])] = int(m[4])
+    label_lines = ["    " + ",".join(map(str, labels[i:i+20]))
+                   for i in range(0, len(labels), 20)]
+    label_data = ",\n".join(label_lines)
+    helpers = f'''
+/-- One local-equation theorem specializes to every generated step. -/
+private theorem natural_step (p : Fin {fixed} → R) (x : Fin 9 → R)
+    (i : Fin {length}) :
+    naturalRegister p x i.val =
+      ({circuit}.naturalNodes.getD i.val (.literal 0)).evalAt p x
+        (naturalRegister p x) :=
+  run_node_equation p x {circuit}.naturalNodes {circuit}.natural_topological i.val
+    (by simpa only [{circuit}.natural_length] using i.isLt)
+
+/-- Zero marks a register with no asserted pure-power specification. -/
+private def naturalPowerLabels : List ℕ :=
+  [
+{label_data}
+  ]
+
+private def naturalPowerLabel (i : ℕ) : ℕ := naturalPowerLabels.getD i 0
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 12000000 in
+private theorem natural_power_certificate : ∀ i : Fin {length},
+    i.val ≠ {base} → naturalPowerLabel i.val ≠ 0 →
+      PowerStep {circuit}.naturalNodes naturalPowerLabel i.val := by
+  decide +kernel
+
+/-- Reuses the existing generic soundness theorem for exponent labels. -/
+private theorem natural_power (p : Fin {fixed} → R) (x : Fin 9 → R)
+    (i : Fin {length}) (hi : naturalPowerLabel i.val ≠ 0) :
+    naturalRegister p x i.val = naturalRegister p x {base} ^ naturalPowerLabel i.val :=
+  run_power p x {circuit}.naturalNodes {circuit}.natural_topological
+    naturalPowerLabel {base} (by decide)
+    (fun j hj => natural_power_certificate
+      ⟨j, by simpa only [{circuit}.natural_length] using hj⟩)
+    i.val (by simpa only [{circuit}.natural_length] using i.isLt) hi
+'''
+    source = source.replace("import DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticDAGSemantics",
+                            "import DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticDAGPowers", 1)
+    source = source.replace("Generated by tools/", "Refactor candidate; original generator tools/", 1)
+    source = source.replace("All results follow from", "Intended proofs use", 1)
+    source = source.replace("theorem natural_step_0", helpers + "\ntheorem natural_step_0", 1)
+    pattern = (r"  run_node_equation p x " + circuit + r"\.naturalNodes " +
+               circuit + r"\.natural_topological (\d+)\n" +
+               r"    \(by rw \[" + circuit + r"\.natural_length\];decide\)")
+    source, nsteps = re.subn(pattern,
+        lambda m: f"  natural_step p x ⟨{m[1]}, by decide⟩", source)
+    assert nsteps == length, (module, nsteps)
+    source, npowers = power_re.subn(lambda m:
+        f"theorem natural_power_{m[1]} {m[2]} :=\n"
+        f"  natural_power p x ⟨{m[1]}, by decide⟩ (by decide)\n", source)
+    assert npowers == len(matches)
+    return source, nsteps, npowers
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("repo", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    patch = []
+    stats = []
+    for module, circuit, fixed, length, base in FAMILIES:
+        rel = Path("Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency") / (module + ".lean")
+        before = (args.repo / rel).read_text()
+        after, steps, powers = render(before, module, circuit, fixed, length, base)
+        target = args.output / rel
+        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        target.write_text(after)
+        patch.extend(difflib.unified_diff(before.splitlines(True), after.splitlines(True),
+                     fromfile="a/" + str(rel), tofile="b/" + str(rel)))
+        stats.append({"file": str(rel), "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(before.encode()).hexdigest(),
+                      "candidate_sha256": hashlib.sha256(after.encode()).hexdigest(),
+                      "source_lines": len(before.splitlines()),
+                      "candidate_lines": len(after.splitlines()),
+                      "source_nonblank_lines": sum(bool(s.strip()) for s in before.splitlines()),
+                      "candidate_nonblank_lines": sum(bool(s.strip()) for s in after.splitlines()),
+                      "public_step_statements_preserved": steps,
+                      "public_power_statements_preserved": powers,
+                      "source_ring_calls": len(re.findall(r"^\s*ring$", before, re.M)),
+                      "candidate_ring_calls": len(re.findall(r"^\s*ring$", after, re.M)),
+                      "status": "candidate source; Lean compilation not yet performed"})
+    (args.output / "generated-steps.patch").write_text("".join(patch))
+    (args.output / "generated-steps-metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(stats, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps(stats, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproducible, lexical source census; not a Lean parser or axiom audit.
+
+Usage: python3 inventory.py /path/to/ProveIt /path/to/output-directory
+Nested comments and strings are masked before token/declaration counts.
+Physical line counts include comments and whitespace. No files are modified.
+"""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+def code_only(s):
+    out = list(s)
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(s):
+        start = i
+        if s.startswith('--', i):
+            i = s.find('\n', i)
+            if i < 0:
+                i = len(s)
+        elif s.startswith('/-', i):
+            depth = 1
+            i += 2
+            while i < len(s) and depth:
+                if s.startswith('/-', i): depth += 1; i += 2
+                elif s.startswith('-/', i): depth -= 1; i += 2
+                else: i += 1
+        elif s[i] == '"':
+            i += 1
+            while i < len(s):
+                if s[i] == '\\': i += 2
+                elif s[i] == '"': i += 1; break
+                else: i += 1
+        else:
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        for j in range(start, min(i, len(s))):
+            if out[j] != '\n': out[j] = ' '
+    return ''.join(out)
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument('repo', type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument('output', type=Path)
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    repo = args.repo.resolve()
+    out = args.output.resolve()
+    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    scope = repo / 'Computability/DiophantineConsistency'
+    base = scope / 'Lean'
+    rows, decls = [], []
+    tokens = Counter()
+    imported_by = Counter()
+    tracked = ['omega', 'nlinarith', 'linarith', 'ring', 'ring_nf', 'simp_all',
+               'native_decide', 'sorry', 'admit', 'axiom']
+    for path in sorted(base.rglob('*.lean')):
+        data = path.read_bytes()
+        text = data.decode('utf-8')
+        code = code_only(text)
+        rel = path.relative_to(repo).as_posix()
+        row = dict(path=rel, bytes=len(data), physical_lines=len(text.splitlines()),
+                   nonblank_code_lines=sum(bool(x.strip()) for x in code.splitlines()),
+                   sha256=hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())
+        words = Counter(re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', code))
+        for word in tracked:
+            row[word] = words[word]
+            tokens[word] += words[word]
+        row['maxHeartbeats_settings'] = len(re.findall(r'\bset_option\s+maxHeartbeats\b', code))
+        row['maxRecDepth_settings'] = len(re.findall(r'\bset_option\s+maxRecDepth\b', code))
+        for m in re.finditer(r'^\s*(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable)\s+)*(theorem|lemma)\s+(\S+)', code, re.M):
+            decls.append(dict(path=rel, line=code[:m.start(2)].count('\n')+1, kind=m[1], name=m[2]))
+        for imp in re.findall(r'^import\s+([^\n]+)', code, re.M):
+            for name in imp.split(): imported_by[name] += 1
+        rows.append(row)
+    sha = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
+    extra = sorted(p.relative_to(repo).as_posix() for p in scope.rglob('*.lean') if not p.is_relative_to(base))
+    summary = dict(commit=sha, scope=str(base.relative_to(repo)), files=len(rows),
+        physical_lines=sum(r['physical_lines'] for r in rows),
+        nonblank_code_lines=sum(r['nonblank_code_lines'] for r in rows),
+        bytes=sum(r['bytes'] for r in rows), lexical_theorem_declarations=len(decls),
+        tokens=dict(tokens), maxHeartbeats_settings=sum(r['maxHeartbeats_settings'] for r in rows),
+        maxRecDepth_settings=sum(r['maxRecDepth_settings'] for r in rows),
+        largest_files=sorted(rows, key=lambda r:r['physical_lines'], reverse=True)[:20],
+        most_imported=imported_by.most_common(20),
+        additional_lean_files_outside_maintained_tree=len(extra),
+        interpretation='Lexical census, not elaborated declaration counting, proof-length measurement, or axiom audit.')
+    (out/'inventory_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2)+'\n')
+    (out/'declarations.json').write_text(json.dumps(decls, indent=2)+'\n')
+    (out/'other_lean_paths.txt').write_text('\n'.join(extra)+'\n')
+    with (out/'files.csv').open('w', newline='') as f:
+        writer=csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0])); writer.writeheader(); writer.writerows(rows)
+    print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in summary.items() if k not in ['largest_files','most_imported']}, indent=2))
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Replay checked demonstrations against the pinned ProveIt checkout.
+
+No candidate patches are applied. Default selection comes from validation.json.
+Pass --include-proposals to try unvalidated demonstration files as well.
+"""
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+PIN = '60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c'
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument('repo', type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument('--without-build', action='store_true', help='Reuse existing dependency oleans.')
+    ap.add_argument('--include-proposals', action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=Path('replay-output'))
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    repo=args.repo.resolve(); bundle=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    got=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=repo,text=True).strip()
+    if got != PIN:
+        raise SystemExit(f'Expected commit {PIN}; found {got}. Use an isolated pinned checkout.')
+    if (repo/'lean-toolchain').read_text().strip() != 'leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0':
+        raise SystemExit('The pinned Lean toolchain is required.')
+    args.output=args.output.resolve(); args.output.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+    evidence=json.loads((bundle/'validation/validation.json').read_text())
+    entries=[x for x in evidence['demonstrations'] if x['status']=='compiled' or args.include_proposals]
+    sources=[bundle/x['path'] for x in entries]
+    imports=set()
+    for p in sources:
+        if not p.is_file(): raise SystemExit(f'Missing packaged source: {p}')
+        for line in re.findall(r'^import\s+([^\n]+)',p.read_text(),re.M):
+            imports.update(n for n in line.split() if n.startswith(('DiophantineConsistency.','Diophantine.')))
+    if imports and not args.without_build:
+        with (args.output/'dependencies.log').open('w') as f:
+            rc=subprocess.run(['lake','build',*sorted(imports)],cwd=repo,stdout=f,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).returncode
+        if rc: raise SystemExit(f'Dependency build failed; see {args.output}/dependencies.log')
+    results=[]
+    for entry,p in zip(entries,sources):
+        log=args.output/(p.stem+'.log'); start=time.monotonic()
+        with log.open('w') as f:
+            rc=subprocess.run(['lake','env','lean','-j1',str(p)],cwd=repo,stdout=f,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).returncode
+        text=log.read_text(errors='replace')
+        forbidden=[s for s in ['sorryAx','Lean.ofReduceBool','Lean.ofReduceNat','Lean.trustCompiler','._native.'] if s in text]
+        result=dict(path=entry['path'],exit_code=rc,forbidden_axiom_markers=forbidden,
+                    elapsed_seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start,3),log=str(log))
+        results.append(result); print(json.dumps(result),flush=True)
+    (args.output/'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+'\n')
+    if any(r['exit_code'] or r['forbidden_axiom_markers'] for r in results):
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+if __name__=='__main__': main()

+# Checker, representation, and object-arithmetic review
+
+Reviewed source: `60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c`.
+All module paths below are relative to
+`Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency/`.
+
+## 1. Replace seven custom list inductions with the existing core API
+
+**Ready first step.** Five copies prove that a successful optional lookup is
+list membership; two copies construct an optional-lookup index from membership.
+Lean 4.32.0 already provides exactly the required statements:
+
+```lean
+List.mem_of_getElem? h
+List.getElem?_of_mem h
+```
+
+Locations: `AnnotatedProofChecker.mem_of_lookup` (177-187),
+`AnnotatedRename.lookup_mem` (110-117), `AnnotatedBound.lookup_mem` (50-57),
+`AnnotatedRuleSide.lookup_mem` (18-25) and `exists_lookup` (27-35),
+`AnnotatedAssumption.lookup_mem` (40-47) and `exists_lookup` (49-57).
+Retaining the private wrapper names avoids touching callers. Alternatively,
+delete the wrappers and call the library lemmas directly, but the supplied patch
+chooses the smaller integration change.
+
+`list-library.patch` reduces those seven declarations from 61 to 21 physical
+source lines, a net saving of 40. These counts include their unchanged
+declarations. The exact generic signatures compile in `ListChecks.lean`; its
+axiom audit reports only `propext`. `git apply --check` passed. The patch itself
+has not yet had a complete module/dependency rebuild; the generic checks do not
+establish the state of every dependent module.
+
+This is more than stylistic compression: the repository no longer maintains
+five independent proofs of an ordinary list fact. It does not alter the
+certificate parser, accept invalid parent references, or change a theorem's
+statement.
+
+## 2. Rewrite under primitive recursion instead of proving congruence by induction
+
+**Compiled complete-module replacements.** `ScalarPRCode.Realizes.prec`
+(64-80) and `PRCode.Realizes.prec` (88-104) already have pointwise equations
+for the supplied base and step programs. The existing proofs perform a second
+induction merely to push those equations through `Nat.rec`.
+
+The scalar proof after the unchanged subtype constructor is:
+
+```lean
+  intro packed
+  simp only [eval, Nat.unpaired, p.property, q.property]
+```
+
+The vector proof uses `[eval, p.property, q.property]`. Simplification rewrites
+the base and step *under the recursor*, including its lambda, so the induction
+is unnecessary. The same observation reduces the `.prec` branch of
+`ScalarPROptimizer.eval_optimize` (119-133) to:
+
+```lean
+  | prec f g hf hg =>
+      simp only [optimize, eval_smartPrec, eval, hf, hg]
+```
+
+`pr-congruence.patch` saves 34 physical source lines: proof fragments of
+12, 11 and 15 lines become 1, 1 and 2 lines. All three complete modified source
+files compiled successfully, as did independent `PRProofChecks.lean` examples.
+That file also proves by `rfl` that both replacement `Realizes.prec` definitions
+have the same executable `.val` as their original counterparts. The axiom
+reports contain only standard Lean axioms, but the footprint is not identical:
+the old scalar `prec` is axiom-free, while the shorter proof uses `propext` and
+`Quot.sound`; the old vector `prec` uses only `propext`, while the shorter proof
+also uses `Quot.sound`. The optimizer already used all three standard axioms,
+and its shortened proof retains that set. This is the cost of rewriting under
+a function binder via function extensionality. If preserving the smaller
+footprint is a goal, `RecursorCore.lean` supplies a kernel-checked, axiom-free
+`rec_congr` proved once by a four-line induction; the two callers can reuse that
+lemma instead. The file checks the generic lemma; it does not contain a tested
+replacement patch using that fallback. These tests do not constitute a
+whole-repository rebuild.
+
+## 3. Move assignment transport to the representation boundary
+
+**Checked common lemma and complete modified module.**
+`Representation.reindex` (155-166), `conjunction` (170-198), and `disjunction`
+(202-231) repeatedly prove function extensionality for a renamed natural
+assignment. Conjunction and disjunction each repeat both a left and a right
+version of the same calculation. Moreover, `QuarticCompiler` already has a
+private `assignment_comp` at lines 95-98. The proposal is to generalize and
+expose that existing idea in the earlier `Representation` module, not to add
+another unrelated helper:
+
+```lean
+theorem natAssignment_comp_map
+    (v : sigma' -> Nat) (w : tau' -> Nat)
+    (f : sigma -> sigma') (g : tau -> tau') :
+    natAssignment v w o Sum.map f g =
+      natAssignment (v o f) (w o g) := by
+  funext i
+  cases i <;> rfl
+```
+
+The actual Unicode Lean declaration is in `AssignmentChecks.lean`, which
+compiled and passed the standard-axiom audit. Then `Expr.eval_rename` and the
+new lemma directly normalize the assignments. Use an explicit `simp only`
+list at these proof sites first; a global simplifier attribute is not required.
+
+`assignment-map.patch` preserves all witness counts and expressions and
+changes their correctness proofs. It saves 25 lines in the whole module,
+including the cost of the new general lemma. After a missing cached dependency was repaired, the complete modified module
+compiled successfully with the pinned compiler and explicit dependency path.
+The initial wrapper processes were stopped and the final direct compiler check
+returned exit code 0. No downstream integration rebuild is claimed.
+
+## 4. Share the scanner's iteration algebra without changing its executable code
+
+The same `fuel.rec initial (fun _ acc => step acc)` appears in
+`AnnotatedRenameScan` (29-55), `AnnotatedBoundScan` (25-48),
+`AnnotatedLineScan` (32-57), and `AnnotatedContext` (91-119).
+Each separately proves zero absorption, movement of the first step out of a
+successor-length run, and retention of a completed state.
+
+`ScannerCore.lean` proves three recursor-level facts once: `rec_fixed`,
+`rec_succ_left`, and `rec_invariant`. It imports only `Init`; all three compile
+on Lean 4.32.0 and their audits report no axioms. For example, an existing
+`scan_zero` can keep its statement and become a direct application of
+`rec_fixed step 0 step_zero fuel`; `scan_done` is the same lemma with the
+appropriate terminal state. Existing scanner definitions can remain literally
+unchanged, because their recursors are definitionally the expressions in the
+lemmas. This avoids perturbing program size theorems or the supplied PR code.
+
+The next, larger change is to isolate a one-step invariant and use
+`rec_invariant` for `AnnotatedLineScan.scan_sound` (59-88). Its raw-input
+invariant must still include the absorbing zero state and a history consisting
+of actual provable judgments. The complete-list simulation in renaming and
+bound scanning also has nearly identical induction structure, but that should
+be a separate refactor with an explicit code/row correspondence. The core
+lemma checks do not certify this larger refactor or claim a measured net line
+saving after integration.
+
+## 5. Strengthen the numeric classifier API from acceptance to value equality
+
+`AnnotatedRenameLocal` and `AnnotatedBoundLocal` already prove both that
+`localCheck` is zero or one and that its value is one exactly when a Boolean
+row validator accepts. Later `step_cons` proofs reconstruct the rejecting case
+from these two facts. See `AnnotatedRenameScan.step_cons` (57-69) and the
+parallel `AnnotatedBoundScan.step_cons`.
+
+Combine the facts once into the stronger reusable conclusion
+`localCheck ... = truth (valid ...)`. The general lemma in `BooleanCore.lean`
+states that `n=0 or n=1` plus `(n=1 iff b=true)` determines
+`n = if b then 1 else 0`. It compiles with only `Init` and reports `propext`.
+The scanner proof can then rewrite the numeric value directly before splitting
+on the Boolean. This removes the negative-acceptance proof and repeated
+`resolve_right` argument at each use.
+
+Keep both premises: knowing only `n=1 iff b=true` does not determine `n` on a
+rejecting input. Also keep the existing raw-natural Booleanity theorem; the
+new equality theorem at encoded rows does not replace raw-code soundness.
+The generic lemma is checked; the full scanner rewrites remain proposals.
+
+## 6. Transport definable induction once, retaining the formula witness
+
+The `Object*` modules repeatedly use `omega_ind` through an explicitly supplied
+formula and its satisfaction equivalence. Examples include
+`ObjectAdditionLaws.addRel_succ_left` (52-72), `addRel_comm` (86-105),
+`addRel_assoc` (126-150), `ObjectMultiplicationLaws`, and `ObjectDistributivity`.
+Their algebraic induction steps are meaningful; the repeated `Sat`/semantic
+predicate conversions are administrative.
+
+Add a lemma `omega_ind_of_spec` whose parameters include an actual `phi : Form`,
+an environment `e`, and `forall n, Sat mem (scons n e) phi iff P n`.
+It transports the base and successor hypotheses through that equivalence,

+This review proposes changes; it does not assert a new consistency endpoint.
+
+## 1. Use the existing power certificate for the generated power lemmas
+
+**Priority: high.** `ArithmeticDAGPowers.lean:24-42` already proves `run_power`:
+numeric labels, checked multiplication edges, and the existing topology imply
+all labelled registers are powers of the designated base. The generated
+`GapCircuitSteps66.lean:2436-3120` instead has 86 individual power proofs, and
+`SplitCircuitSteps59.lean:2591-3443` has 107. Every one invokes `ring` after
+rewriting previously proved power facts. This is duplicated proof work, rather
+than a need for a new power-reasoning framework.
+
+Emit an exponent-label list, one closed `PowerStep` certificate proved by
+`decide +kernel`, and a private specialization of `run_power`. Preserve all
+193 public theorem names and their exact types as one-line applications. In
+the split family, `SplitJointPower59.lean` already carries the parent labels
+and a private `natural_old_steps` theorem. In an integrated refactor, extract
+that shared data/certificate into an upstream label module imported by both
+Steps and JointPower; do not import a later recipe module and introduce a cycle.
+
+Existing example:
+
+```lean
+theorem natural_power_25 (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) :
+    naturalRegister p x 25 = naturalRegister p x 20 ^ 4 := by
+  rw [natural_step_25]
+  simp only [natural_power_24]
+  ring
+```
+
+Candidate after introducing the shared certified helper:
+
+```lean
+theorem natural_power_25 (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) :
+    naturalRegister p x 25 = naturalRegister p x 20 ^ 4 :=
+  natural_power p x ⟨25, by decide⟩ (by decide)
+```
+
+The label zero is a sentinel for “no asserted power specification,” not a
+claim that the value equals the zeroth power. Keep that interpretation and
+the nonzero-label premise. Prove the certificate against the actual stored
+node list, not against a second unlinked copy. This changes proof structure
+without changing the circuit, operation count, or polynomial.

+## 2. Share the specialization of `run_node_equation`

+**Priority: high, low architectural risk.** `GapCircuitSteps66.lean` contains
+484 `natural_step_*` declarations, `SplitCircuitSteps59.lean` contains 515.
+Their proof bodies all call the same general theorem, repeat the same circuit
+and topology constants, rewrite the same length, and decide one bound.

+Define one circuit-specific theorem taking `i : Fin 484` or `Fin 515`, with
+right side `(nodes.getD i.val (.literal 0)).evalAt p x (naturalRegister p x)`.
+The existing explicit public equations then have bodies such as
+`natural_step p x ⟨10, by decide⟩`. Keeping their public types explicitly
+spelled out preserves good rewrite behaviour and human-readable interfaces.

+The prepared candidate combines ideas 1 and 2. Measured source changes are:

+# Digit, carry, and current-cell proof simplifications
+
+Reviewed snapshot: `60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c`.
+All source paths below are relative to
+`Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency/`.
+No original repository source was changed. The proposals preserve the existing
+mathematical boundaries: sparse support is not occupation, at-most-one is not
+exactly-one, and phase recovery must not be used as its own premise.
+
+## Checked deliverables
+
+`HalfShiftArithmetic.lean` and `NormalizationArithmetic.lean` compile under
+Lean 4.32.0 with `import Std.Tactic`, without Mathlib or repository imports.
+The corresponding `.check.log` files record successful `#print axioms` output.
+Across their six theorems, the only axioms reported are `propext` and
+`Quot.sound`. No `sorryAx`, native decision axiom, or extra source axiom occurs.
+These are checked reusable arithmetic lemmas. The wrappers in the original
+project and the separate candidate patches require project-level compilation;
+do not describe every proposed integration as checked on this evidence alone.
+
+## 1. Put a conditional witness inside the branch that needs it
+
+**Priority: high; small API change with a concrete two-file patch.**
+
+`NativePreliminaryCount2011.total_le_one_all_phases` (lines 61--87) receives
+`u : Nat -> Nat` globally, even though `u` is used only in the middle-phase
+branch `7 <= phase <= 10`. The literal caller in
+`CurrentCount2011.count_le_one_of_middle_padding` (lines 32--64) consequently
+manufactures a global `u` by a case split (lines 46--54): it extracts the real
+padding witness in the middle branch and chooses a dummy zero function outside
+that branch.
+
+Change the generic theorem to accept
+
+```lean
+(hpadding : 7 ≤ phase → phase ≤ 10 → ∃ u : ℕ → ℕ,
+  ... u ...)
+```
+
+and destruct `u` only after entering the middle branch. Then the caller can
+pass its existing `hpadding` directly; the entire dummy-witness block and its
+local `classical` disappear. The logical strength of the actual application is
+unchanged: no additional padding premise is introduced. In fact the generic
+API expresses its genuinely conditional data dependency more accurately.
+
+`conditional-padding.patch` implements this change against the exact snapshot.
+The two original files total 155 physical lines; the proposed files total 145.
+The core theorem's line count stays 89, while the caller changes from 66 to 56.
+`ConditionalPadding.lean` gives the proposed generic theorem under a fresh name,
+so it can be tested without replacing the original theorem. The patched caller
+still needs compilation with the changed generic theorem. Repository search
+found one production call of `total_le_one_all_phases`, plus a `#print axioms`
+check and documentation references. If an external user needs the old API,
+retain it temporarily as a short wrapper that supplies `⟨u, hpadding ...⟩`;
+that compatibility option has a different source-line total.
+
+## 2. Use the existing stronger congruence at smaller moduli
+
+**Priority: high; six lines saved in one proof body without new mathematics.**
+
+`CurrentClause2011.reflected_weight_mod` (lines 122--130) already classifies
+every reflected coefficient modulo 2048. `CurrentEarlyPadding2011` repeats
+the same five-way constructor split and finite label-position case checks in
+its private `reflected_mod_sixteen` (lines 99--107).
+
+Since 16 divides 2048, use
+
+```lean
+exact (CurrentClause2011.reflected_weight_mod e).of_dvd
+  (by decide : 16 ∣ 2048)
+```
+
+The local `selectorUnit` definitions have identical equations, so this proposal
+uses definitional equality and does not require making the older private
+definition public. A small shared public definition would also work, but is
+not necessary for this patch. The old proof body has seven physical lines; the
+replacement has one. `modulus-reuse.patch` and `ModulusReuse.lean` provide the
+exact patch and a standalone candidate theorem. At the time of this note's
+initial preparation, this integration has not been compiled because it needs
+the full `CurrentClause2011` dependency chain.
+
+The same principle suggests proving coefficient residues once at the largest
+relevant power of two, then using `Nat.ModEq.of_dvd` for lower phases. This
+avoids independently maintained finite classifications. It does not justify
+discarding higher coefficients, collisions, or carries from the actual word.
+
+## 3. Normalize exact digit/carry equations through a small scalar API
+
+**Priority: high; generic arithmetic helpers compiled.**
+
+Repeated proofs start from
+
+```lean
+raw = digit + radix * carry
+```
+
+and then recover either a quotient, a residue, or a carry reset. Examples:
+
+- `CurrentClause2011.normalized_clause_residue`, lines 160--166: residue modulo
+  2048, using divisibility of the radix.
+- `CurrentEarlyPadding2011.padding_digit_residue`, lines 251--258: the same
+  arithmetic modulo 16.
+- `CurrentPhaseParity2011.marker_digit_parity`, lines 113--117: modulo 2.
+- `CurrentEarlyPadding2011.early_carry_zero`, lines 88--93: the raw budget
+  lies below one radix, so the outgoing carry vanishes.
+
+The checked `NormalizationArithmetic.lean` proves:
+
+```lean
+quotient_of_decomposition
+  (hd : digit < radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) :
+  carry = raw / radix
+
+residue_of_decomposition
+  (hm : modulus ∣ radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) :
+  digit % modulus = raw % modulus
+
+zero_carry_of_decomposition
+  (hsmall : raw < radix) (h : raw = digit + radix * carry) :
+  carry = 0
+```
+
+This separates the genuine problem-specific work (the raw coefficient budget,
+the reflected residue, or support exclusion) from boilerplate natural-number
+division. The residue helper needs no digit bound; the quotient helper does.
+The zero-carry helper needs no independently supplied digit bound, because the
+small raw total and nonnegativity already give it.
+
+There is also a record-level simplification. `CurrentPolynomialWindow2011.Facts`
+already exists and should be retained, rather than replaced by another giant
+bundle. Its `carry_recurrence` field (lines 60--62) follows from `digit_bound`
+(59) and `carry_equation` (63--66). After adding the generic helper, make
+`Facts.carry_recurrence` a derived theorem with the same dot-notation API.
+Consumers can keep calling `h.carry_recurrence`; constructors no longer carry
+two proofs of the same normalization. Do not remove recurrence from other
+interfaces that do not supply a strict digit bound: the equation alone does
+not imply the quotient recurrence.
+
+## 4. Replace half-radix case enumeration by an exact quotient/remainder formula
+
+**Priority: medium-high; arithmetic kernel compiled, source integration pending.**
+
+`NativeCyclicRotation.shiftDigits_half_bound` (lines 100--116) splits the current
+digit into four cases, then separately bounds the predecessor quotient.
+`shiftDigits_half_parity_89` (lines 160--165) enumerates all 16 current/predecessor
+combinations. The exact formula is shorter and exposes why both facts hold:
+
+\[
+ (sa)\bmod(2s)+\lfloor sb/(2s)\rfloor
+   =s(a\bmod2)+\lfloor b/2\rfloor,\qquad s>0.
+\]
+
+The checked `HalfShiftArithmetic.lean` derives this using
+`Nat.mul_mod_mul_left` and `Nat.mul_div_mul_left`, then proves both the bound
+and parity statement. The bound even needs only `b <= 3`; the current digit
+`a` can be arbitrary. For parity, also require `s % 2 = 0`. To recover the
+existing 89-bit lemma, instantiate `s = 2^88`, use `2^89 = 2 * 2^88`, and unfold
+`shiftDigits`. The cyclic predecessor stays exactly `k - 1`. No boundary digit
+or half-phase is silently discarded.
+
+This is preferable to replacing the 16 cases with opaque automation: the new
+formula supports future radix changes and makes the carry contribution visible.
+`NativeBooleanRotation.rotation_eq_scaled` already supplies the corresponding
+Boolean no-overflow theorem; do not duplicate or replace it with the weaker
+three-valued half-radix bound.
+
+## 5. Put field-coordinate and off-origin mask lemmas below the clause layer
+
+**Priority: medium; architectural proposal, not yet implemented.**
+
+The source repeats two steps: compute the field residue of an aligned cell plus
+an offset, then prove the point cannot be the global origin before using the
+high-mask lookup.
+
+- `CurrentClause2011.clause_target_residue` / `clause_mask`: lines 41--54.
+- `CurrentPhaseParity2011.marker_target_residue` / `marker_mask`: 27--41.
+- `CurrentEarlyPadding2011.padding_target_residue` / `padding_mask`: 263--281.
+
+Introduce a shared lemma for `b.val % 2011 = 0` and `e < 2011`:
+
+```lean
+(b + (e : ZMod (N * 2011))).val % 2011 = e
+```
+
+and a high-mask specialization for `0 < e`:
+
+```lean
+maskDigits (b + (e : ZMod (N * 2011))) = cellDigit e
+```
+
+The three masks become a shared lookup plus `cellDigit_clause`,
+`cellDigit_marker`, or `cellDigit_padding`. A generic source-offset residue
+lemma also replaces the parallel `he`, `h18`, `h2020` derivations in
+`clause_convolution` (65--90) and `marker_convolution` (51--76).
+
+The dependency placement is essential: `CurrentCellTranslation2011` currently
+imports `CurrentClause2011`, so importing its existing `source_residue` into the
+clause module would create a cycle. Move only the low-level residue/coordinate
+definitions into a small upstream module; keep decoding and coefficient data
+above it. `source_residue` already handles arbitrary temporal shifts and both
+wrap regimes, so reuse its mathematics. Do not add an artificial `t < N*2011`
+restriction. Retain the nonzero full cyclic modulus, the distinction between
+natural and group subtraction, the off-origin condition, and the `N = 1` case.
+
+## 6. Share the origin-decrement word lemma across the two high-mask families
+
+**Priority: medium; concrete mathematical interface, not yet compiled.**
+
+`CurrentHighDigits2011.high_mask_word` (107--126) and
+`NativeHighPort54.mask_word` (182--202) independently prove that subtracting one
+from the origin digit subtracts one from the whole word, with no borrow into a
+neighbor. Abstract this part as
+
+```lean
+theorem word_sub_origin (r delta : ℕ) (a : ZMod n → ℕ)
+    (hdelta : delta ≤ a 0) :
+    word r (fun k => a k - if k = 0 then delta else 0) =
+      word r a - delta
+```
+
+Prove the pointwise additive reconstruction using `Nat.sub_add_cancel`, then
+apply `word_add` and the already-existing `word_origin`. Each concrete high-mask
+proof is then its existing periodic-word identity plus this helper. This
+keeps the no-borrow hypothesis explicit. It must not be generalized to arbitrary
+pointwise subtraction without proving the corresponding pointwise bounds.
+The source already has `word_origin`, `word_add`, `word_periodic`, and
+`periodic_factor`; the proposal fills the small missing composition rather than
+reproving those existing abstractions.
+
+## 7. Expose the already-proved physical sum identity directly
+
+**Priority: medium; small API improvement.**
+
+`CurrentClause2011.selectorCount_eq_prefix` (110--116) first proves
+
+```lean
+selectorCount c b = ∑ p : Fin 942, c (b + (p.val : ZMod (N * 2011)))
+```
+
+using the actual `physicalEquiv`, then converts to a natural prefix sum. Make
+that first equality a public named lemma too. `CurrentOneHot2011` (68--71) and
+`CurrentFieldOffsets2011` (88--93) currently travel through the prefix-sum form
+and back to the `Fin` sum. They can use the direct equality with `simpa only`.
+This is not a proposal to assume an arbitrary sorting permutation: the
+authoritative `physicalEquiv` and its proof remain the basis of the theorem.
+Choose one rewrite direction and avoid adding both directions to the global
+simp set.
+
+## 8. Factor the restored canonical window once, preserving its witness
+
+**Priority: medium-long term; shared interface proposal.**
+
+`CurrentSparseDigits2011.polynomial_zero_reconstructs` (118--129) and
+`CurrentHighDigits2011.polynomial_zero_mask_test` (141--152) repeat evaluation
+conversion, the Carrier65-to-Carrier66 restore, canonical-window extraction,
+and the same power normalization. A lower-level lemma in
+`CurrentCarrierArithmetic2011` or a new upstream source-window module can
+produce the restored source, one positive `N`, and both low/high arithmetic
+mask tests. The Boolean and high-digit modules then specialize it.
+
+The important issue is witness coherence, not just shorter text. Downstream
+composition must use the same restored source and same `N`; independently
+combining two existential statements requires a uniqueness argument.
+`CurrentPolynomialWindow2011.polynomial_zero_window` already constructs a
+coherent source and window (78--152). Preserve that success and extract only
+the genuinely duplicated lower-level portion. Do not replace this by a
+package containing desired future tile occupation or machine semantics.
+
+## What to leave alone
+
+- `CurrentHighDigits2011.cellDigit_formula` already proves a symbolic ten-block
+  formula instead of 2011 separate digit cases. It is a good abstraction.
+- `NativeCyclicCarry.exists_bounded_carries` already uses a monotone fixed point
+  on a bounded carry box, so no cyclic starting point is assumed. Its proof is
+  short; replacing it with a handwritten iteration would add complexity.
